1#include "COINAlgebra/Core/DecayLevel.h"
2#include "COINAlgebra/Core/DecayTransition.h"
3#include "COINAlgebra/Core/DecayPath.h"

5#include "COINAlgebra/Core/DecayVector.h"
6#include "COINAlgebra/Algebra/PathAlgebra.h"

16void example_vector()
17{
18    std::cout
19        << "============================================\n"
20        << "       COINAlgebra Vector Example\n"
21        << "============================================\n\n";
22
23
24    // ========================================================
25    // 1. Construct five-level quiver
26    // ========================================================
27
28    DecayQuiver quiver;
29
30    DecayLevel* d0 =
31        quiver.AddLevel("d0");
32
33    DecayLevel* d1 =
34        quiver.AddLevel("d1");
35
36    DecayLevel* d2 =
37        quiver.AddLevel("d2");
38
39    DecayLevel* d3 =
40        quiver.AddLevel("d3");
41
42    DecayLevel* d4 =
43        quiver.AddLevel("d4");
44
45
46    // ========================================================
47    // 2. Construct fully connected decay quiver
48    //
49    // Every excited level has a transition to every lower
50    // level.
51    //
52    // The outgoing probabilities from each level sum to one.
53    // ========================================================
54
55    // d4 -> d0, d1, d2, d3
56
57    quiver.AddTransition(
58        "gamma40",
59        d4,
60        d0,
61        0.10
62    );
63
64    quiver.AddTransition(
65        "gamma41",
66        d4,
67        d1,
68        0.20
69    );
70
71    quiver.AddTransition(
72        "gamma42",
73        d4,
74        d2,
75        0.30
76    );
77
78    quiver.AddTransition(
79        "gamma43",
80        d4,
81        d3,
82        0.40
83    );
84
85
86    // d3 -> d0, d1, d2
87
88    quiver.AddTransition(
89        "gamma30",
90        d3,
91        d0,
92        0.20
93    );
94
95    quiver.AddTransition(
96        "gamma31",
97        d3,
98        d1,
99        0.30
100    );
101
102    DecayTransition* g32 = quiver.AddTransition(
103        "gamma32",
104        d3,
105        d2,
106        0.50
107    );
108
109
110    // d2 -> d0, d1
111
112    quiver.AddTransition(
113        "gamma20",
114        d2,
115        d0,
116        0.30
117    );
118
119   DecayTransition* g21 =  quiver.AddTransition(
120        "gamma21",
121        d2,
122        d1,
123        0.70
124    );
125
126
127    // d1 -> d0
128
129    DecayTransition* g10 = quiver.AddTransition(
130        "gamma10",
131        d1,
132        d0,
133        1.00
134    );
135
136
137    // ========================================================
138    // 3. Print quiver
139    // ========================================================
140
141    std::cout
142        << "Quiver:\n\n";
143
144    quiver.Print();
145
146
147    // ========================================================
148    // 4. Construct stationary paths
149    //
150    // e_i : d_i -> d_i
151    //
152    // These have:
153    //
154    //     Length()       = 0
155    //     IsStationary() = true
156    //     GetProbability() = 1
157    //
158    // The probability is one because the probability is the
159    // empty product for a length-zero path.
160    // ========================================================
161
162    DecayPath e0(d0);
163    DecayPath e1(d1);
164    DecayPath e2(d2);
165    DecayPath e3(d3);
166    DecayPath e4(d4);
167
168
169    // ========================================================
170    // 5. Construct the decay vector
171    //
172    // Stationary coefficients are initial branching populations,
173    // chosen below to sum to one. Single-transition coefficients
174    // equal their intrinsic transition probabilities:
175    //
176    //     coefficient(transition) = path.GetProbability()
177    // ========================================================
178
179    DecayVector decay_vector;
180
181
182    // --------------------------------------------------------
183    // Stationary components
184    // --------------------------------------------------------
185
186    decay_vector.AddTerm(
187        e0,
188        0.10 //e0.GetProbability()
189    );
190
191    decay_vector.AddTerm(
192        e1,
193        0.20 //e1.GetProbability()
194    );
195
196    decay_vector.AddTerm(
197        e2,
198        0.30 // e2.GetProbability()
199    );
200
201    decay_vector.AddTerm(
202        e3,
203        0.25 //e3.GetProbability()
204    );
205
206    decay_vector.AddTerm(
207        e4,
208        0.15 //e4.GetProbability()
209    );
210
211
212    // --------------------------------------------------------
213    // Length-one components
214    // --------------------------------------------------------
215
216    for(const auto* transition :
217        quiver.GetTransitions())
218    {
219        DecayPath path(*transition);
220
221        decay_vector.AddTerm(
222            path,
223            path.GetProbability()
224        );
225    }
226
227
228    // ========================================================
229    // 6. Print stationary paths
230    // ========================================================
231
232    std::cout
233        << "\n============================================\n"
234        << "          STATIONARY PATHS\n"
235        << "============================================\n\n";
236
237    for(const auto& level :
238        quiver.GetLevels())
239    {
240        DecayPath path(level);
241
242        std::cout
243            << std::left
244            << std::setw(12)
245            << path.ToString()
246            << " length = "
247            << std::setw(3)
248            << path.Length()
249            << " probability = "
250            << path.GetProbability()
251            << "\n";
252    }
253
254
255    // ========================================================
256    // 7. Print length-one paths
257    // ========================================================
258
259    std::cout
260        << "\n============================================\n"
261        << "           LENGTH-ONE PATHS\n"
262        << "============================================\n\n";
263
264    for(const auto* transition :
265        quiver.GetTransitions())
266    {
267        DecayPath path(*transition);
268
269        std::cout
270            << std::left
271            << std::setw(35)
272            << path.ToString()
273            << " P = "
274            << std::setprecision(10)
275            << path.GetProbability()
276            << "\n";
277    }
278
279
280    // ========================================================
281    // 8. Print complete vector
282    // ========================================================
283
284    std::cout
285        << "\n============================================\n"
286        << "       PROBABILITY-WEIGHTED VECTOR\n"
287        << "============================================\n\n";
288
289    decay_vector.Print();
290
291
292    // ========================================================
293    // 9. Summary
294    // ========================================================
295
296    std::cout
297        << "\n============================================\n"
298        << "                  SUMMARY\n"
299        << "============================================\n\n";
300
301    std::cout
302        << "Number of levels: "
303        << quiver.GetLevels().size()
304        << "\n";
305
306    std::cout
307        << "Number of transitions: "
308        << quiver.GetTransitions().size()
309        << "\n";
310
311    std::cout
312        << "Number of stationary paths: 5\n";
313
314    std::cout
315        << "Number of length-one paths: "
316        << quiver.GetTransitions().size()
317        << "\n";
318
319    std::cout
320        << "Number of vector terms: "
321        << decay_vector.Size()
322        << "\n";
323
324    std::cout
325        << "Expected number of vector terms: 15\n";
326
327    std::cout
328        << "\n============================================\n";
329    // ========================================================
330    // 10. Probability vector in the coincidence algebra
331    //
332    // Split d = b + tau, then compute P = b *d tau in C_d.
333    // For a branch e_i and transition p, the coefficient is
334    // b_i c_d(e_i,p) tau_p: initial population times the sum
335    // of connecting-path weights times the transition weight.
336    //
337    // A separated branching level remains a stationary tensor
338    // factor, preserving where the decay started. If it is the
339    // transition's source, the local identity reduces e_i tensor p
340    // to p. Every resulting term has coincidence degree one.
341    // ========================================================
342
343    PathProjectors projectors;
344    DecayVector branching_vector =
345        projectors.BranchingProjector(decay_vector);
346    DecayVector transition_vector = decay_vector - branching_vector;
347
348    // Explicit physical order, highest first. In this fully connected
349    // quiver this also orders levels by decreasing outgoing-arrow count.
350    CAlgebra coincidence_algebra(quiver, {d4, d3, d2, d1, d0}, decay_vector);
351    CAlgebra::Vector probability_vector = coincidence_algebra.Multiply(
352        coincidence_algebra.Embed(branching_vector),
353        coincidence_algebra.Embed(transition_vector)
354    );
355
356    std::cout
357        << "\n============================================\n"
358        << "     COINCIDENCE PROBABILITY VECTOR\n"
359        << "              P = b *d tau\n"
360        << "============================================\n\n"
361        << std::left << std::setw(18) << "Coefficient"
362        << "Coincidence basis\n";
363
364    for (const auto& term : probability_vector)
365    {
366        std::cout
367            << std::left << std::setw(18) << std::setprecision(10)
368            << term.coefficient << term.coin.ToString() << "\n";
369    }
370    std::cout << "Number of probability-vector terms: "
371              << probability_vector.size() << "\n";
372
373    // ========================================================
374    // 11. Existing path-algebra probability calculations
375    //
376    // FeedingVector combines contributions from all initial branches
377    // for each transition. P above retains the separate branch factors.
378    // ========================================================
379
380    PathAlgebra algebra(quiver);
381    DecayProbability pb(algebra,projectors);
382    DecayVector feedingVector = pb.FeedingVector(decay_vector);
383    feedingVector.PrintTable();
384    DecayPath pathi(*g32);
385    DecayPath pathj(*g10);
386    double prob = pb.FeedingProbability(decay_vector,pathi);
387    double coin = pb.CoincidenceProbability(decay_vector,pathi, pathj);
388    std::cout << prob <<"\n";
389    std::cout << coin <<"\n";
390}
